question.text: Phenol on treatment with <math><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow><mi>O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> in the presence of NaOH followed by acidification produces compound X as the major product. X on treatment with <math><msub><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>C</mi><msub><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi>C</mi><mi>O</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>O in the presence of catalytic amount of <math><msub><mrow><mi>H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi>S</mi><msub><mrow><mi>O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> produces:

solution.text:
Two different reactions are taking place here Kolbe–Schmitt reaction and esterification reaction (treatment of the product of Kolbe–Schmitt reaction with (CH3CO)2O (ester). 

The two reactions can be written as follows:

1.Kolbe–Schmitt reaction: reaction of phenol with carbon dioxide in the presence of sodium hydroxide, followed by acidification converts phenol to 1−1− hydroxybenzoic acid (Salicylic acid).

 

2.Esterification reaction: The salicylic acid is then reacted with acetic anhydride (CH3CO)2O) to form aspirin.
